(Rolasa starts to scoop her smashed merchandise from the floor.) S-Sure thing, outlander. I buy my hides from House Hlaalu now. I'll buy all my supplies through them. Please just calm down...
Please, stop smashing my potions all over the floor!
A duel? To the....death? I...ah... w-withdraw the st-statements I made against House Redoran. Yes. Very much so.
There's no need for that, %PCName. We can solve this in a more civilised manner. Here is the gold I owe the Guild. Now please, leave me in peace.
Surely you would not spill the blood of your fellow mer!
You lower races can be so... vulgar. Here, take your gold and leave me to my studies.
Let us not stoop to that, please.
Alright, %PCName. Just put the blade away. I'll join the Mages Guild, keep my head. Everyone's happy, eh?
Alright, %PCName. No need to break my neck, no ser. I'll join the Mages Guild. Everyone's happy, eh?
Alright, %PCName. Just put the axe down. I'll join the Mages Guild, and keep my head in the bargain. Everyone's happy, eh?
(Ilarar licks his lips nervously.) It's not so simple as that. Mistress Dratha would put a writ on my head. I'd be a dead man.
This is Telvanni territory. You...you wouldn't dare.
No idea. Sounds like an Ashlander name. They have camps all over the grazelands around here.
Keep your voice down, or I'll call for the Ordinators.
Toothless words, from a toothless House.
You act like a crude barbarian, %PCName. Speak in a manner that befits your breeding.
Don't threaten me, peasant. I can defend myself against the likes of you.
Keep a civil tongue in my tower, or I'll turn your bones to ash.
I had no idea you had the same passion for adaptive response formula that I do, %PCName! I would be more than happy to make a donation of 2000 septims to a fellow scholar.
You are wise to say so. There are too few who appreciate the importance of the research I do here.
Perhaps you are right, %PCName. The resources of your Guild would truly further my research. I shall sign up next time I travel through Balmora.
It is true, I deserve better than this rat-infested outpost. And they call this a reward for my loyal service...
My powers are indeed great, %PCName. Tell me... more about myself.
I'm not here to give you directions, %PCRace.
Perhaps the %PCRace should find a book on such things, and leave %Name alone.
I fear the wealth of our culture and history would be quite beyond you, outlander.
Ask the local Dunmer - I'm sure they could tell you more.

Although the Telvanni are cunning enchanters and ambitious strategists, they do not respect our traditions, nor properly venerate the Tribunal, blessed be thy names. Their wizards-lords claim might makes right - yet they augment their natural lifespan allotted to us Dunmer through foul magics - and some are even rumored to consort with vampires. We of House Redoran understand that with strength comes responsibility, and that we must honor the Gods, then our clan, before we look to serve ourselves.

House Telvanni prefers isolation to integration, believing the purity of separation makes them strong. Though their wizard-lords are powerful, their ears are deaf to opportunity, and the possibility of the new. They lack the vision to see which way the winds of change are blowing, growing strange and bitter in their mushroom towers.

The Telvani don't welcome visitors. My business contacts there are mostly outsiders - Hlaalu and Citizens in the foreign districts of port centers. Their townfolk are formal and humorless. But if you mean the High Telvani wizards, the so-called Parliament of Bugs - yes, it is near-impossible for outsiders to meet with their wizards. They all deal through servants, slaves, and agents, local or foreign-trained.

It's easy enough to unlock a chest with a simple spell. But what if some cunning fetcher has rigged it with a trap, too? Then telekinesis is your friend. Blast the chest from a safe distance to set off any nasty surprises - and don't forget to duck.

A rival with a cool head and powerful allies is dangerous. Hard to catch them in heat, harder to make them sling the first hex. Strike first, you'll have their friends to deal with and the law to pay off. So. Practice the frenzy spell. Practice till you can make a meditating monk shake with rage. Then force your nemesis to fight, on your terms.

You're an outlander, so perhaps you are free from foolish superstitions about disturbing the dead. But let me warn you. The greater bonewalker will sap your strength with curses, leaving you meek and mewling as a newborn pup. Make sure you have potions or a charm to restore yourself before you go delving into those dusty tombs.

Common wisdom tells you to avoid Kagouti and their tusks like corprus. But where the common mer sees danger, a Telvanni sees opportunity. Simple minds are easy to command with the right magics. And then it will be your foes impaled on those wicked tusks, rather than you.

If a mer's mind is weak enough to be swayed by magic, then they deserve their fate. Is your tower missing a smith to repair your blade, or a bard to entertain your guests? Command them to obey you. They should be honoured to serve one who wields such raw power.

Before you start to forge artifacts infused with your own magic, first practice casting with items enchanted by more experienced hands. The knowledge you glean - the ease of the cast, the sapping of its power - will prove invaluable when it comes to imitating, and then improving upon them with enchantments of your own.

Training is expensive, but it's the easiest way to get ahead without risking your hide in the wild. Dab some bug musk under your ears before you negotiate the price - you'll more than make back your gold after a lesson or two.
Some folk are just born with a silver tongue. Bards and rogues, anyone who thrives by the gift of the gab. Trying to butter them up is tricky - they'll know exactly what you're up to.

Sometimes a pawnbroker will have a rare piece in a poor state, but they lack the skill or material to repair it themselves. You can purchase and polish it up - for a fraction of what it would cost to buy it fresh from the forge.

I bet a smart f'lah like yourself knows not to sell weapons or armour back to the smith with rents and dents. But did you know you can drain magic amulets or rings bone-dry and still profit from an enchanter? Wizards. Booksmart, sure, but not septim-smart.

How do the wealthy become filthy rich? I'll let you in on a real trade secret, chum - they're selling gold. No, I'm not pulling your leg. Selling gold to someone is a formal investment in their shop. If they accept, it means they'll have more gold to purchase your wares that day - and pledge to keep their cash reserve that high in future, in return for repeat business. That can be very lucrative if you plan on doing plenty of future deals with a small number of traders.

Every price in this life is open to negotiation. Every price except a prayer, that is. No, I'm not speaking in riddles - I just mean blessings at Temple shrines are always at fixed fees. Damn those dour priests.

A good strategy is to paralyze your opponent, cast some kind of touch spell that does damage for a while, like poison, then retreat to a farther range to cast your targeted, long range spells. Recast paralyze if the creature isn't dead by the time they reach you again.
Whenever I was sick as a youth, my mother would brew me a bitter tea of lichen and some ash from grandfather's urn. Oh, it tasted as bad as it sounds - but I always felt better the next day.

Most beasts in the wild don't prey on their own. You wouldn't expect it, but that even goes for cliff racers. If you're planning to stay a while around a spot, take what you need from the kills but leave the carcasses right there to rot -- might deter others from swooping in, at least for a time.

Most Dunmer love making a show out of their supposed cultural superiority. If you ever have to do business with a particularly sanctimonious one, let him say his piece and keep your talk focused on the matter at hand. Ignoring veiled insults and racist sentiments is the only way to get along with the natives.

Dunmer are very sensitive about necromancy -- especially when it comes to distinguishing one kind from another. A hedge-wizard conjurer tampering with corpses in a cave? That's bad. Priests raising the dead to guard tombs? Perfectly fine. Don't try to argue that they're the same deal. You'll only end up offending the natives, and in this province that can prove fatal.

You look at the sky like one who's been plagued by cliff racers. If you get attacked on a path you want to travel back through -- leave the carcass in clear view. The pests usually know better than to hang around their dead.

If you're attacked out in the wild, don't try and be a hero unless you've got the proper training. Beat a hasty retreat to civilisation, and let the guards take care of the rest. It's what they're paid for, after all.

A smith will overplay the slightest damage on a weapon when you're offering to sell. But smiths aren't the sharpest tools in the shed either, and you can be smart. Don't let on that you're selling and get it repaired first -- you'll have a much easier time bartering once your blade shines the right way.

We don't like to cut loose and make fools of ourselves after work like some of you outlanders. That cornerclub, for instance - Dirty Muriel's? It's even worse than the name suggests. Drunks, gamblers and rogues, the pack of them.

We don't like to cut loose and make fools of ourselves after work like some of you outlanders. That cornerclub, for instance - The South Wall? Drunks, gamblers and rogues, the pack of them. A 'workers' club, indeed. Just what exactly is it they work at?

We don't like to cut loose and make fools of ourselves after work like some of you outlanders. That tavern, for instance - The Rat in the Pot? Drunks, gamblers and rogues, the pack of them. No self-respecting citizen I know drinks there.

Get your hands on any bonemold gear from the natives? The material's a bit tricky. That said, even if you can't do it yourself, repair fees are a relatively cheap investment. You know how hard it is to bargain with flawed merchandise.
Always try to get a good night's sleep. I'm not your mother, but really - if you haven't got your health, you haven't got anything.

Talk to everyone you meet, of course - it's a fine way to pass the time. But some folk have more to say than others. The savants - either freelance, or working for the Great Houses - they're the most learned scholars and distinguished minds you'll find. If you're in the company of one, keep your mouth closed and your ears open. You'll learn much that way.

Try to sell a weapon to a smith -- they'll grab it, feel its heft, give it a few spins, point out all its flaws and then some, and give you a hard time about it all when it comes to the price, too. Try to sell a weapon to a pawnbroker -- all they'll think about it how much they can sell it for to the smith. And they make a living of it, the traders do, so you better believe they'll take their cut. You want to get the most out of battle spoils? Just skip the middle man.

Travelling along the trails and countryside can be dangerous. The Legion doesn't have enough troops to patrol all the roads, and the Great Houses only look out for their own interests. Take a boat or a silt strider to your destination, if you can afford the fare.
Gather any gear from your fallen enemies? Why not try your hand at repairing the notches you've put there yourself. Makes good practice, and you don't risk damaging your own equipment.

You think we're a conquered people, eh? You smug outlanders know nothing of our history. Vivec, thrice-blessed be his name, knew better than to fight a war against the Empire and the devil Dagoth-Ur at the same time. The Armistice is nothing but a scrap of paper that makes the Emperor our ruler - in name only. And after the Tribunal have defeated Dagoth-Ur and his monsters, they'll take care of Tiber Septim, his legions, and anyone else who thinks they can put their boot on our necks.
I must tell you, all this self-righteous Western clamor against slavery is really tiresome. Our right to own slaves is protected by law -- IMPERIAL law. People who free slaves are breaking the law.

I must tell you, all this self-righteous Western clamor against slavery is really tiresome. Our right to own slaves is protected by law -- IMPERIAL law. People who free slaves are breaking the law. That's why Orvas Dren is hiring bounty hunters to track down these catmen and pondscum. Teach them a lesson.

This isn't the nation my ancestors founded, I tell you. Upstanding Dunmer like Orvas Dren are getting their throats slit in their beds, while that swine Hlaalu Helseth talks as if he will surrender our ancient right to have slaves. Mark my words outlander - when this Emperor dies, his legions are going to be recalled from our lands. And then we'll see who really runs Morrowind.
It's not just the blight storms that are bad this year. They got all sorts of blighted beasts coming down from the mountain. It's pretty dangerous on the trails and in the outback villages.

I've heard rumours of merchants and pilgrims attacked on trails by crazed Dunmer with clubs. Not Ashlanders, mind - but dressed ragged and spouting gibberish all the same. The strangest thing is they don't take gold or goods, so they can't be bandits.

The blight storms have been so bad around Red Mountain this year that the crops and herds of the outlying villages are really suffering. The price of everything is going to go up. There's no easy cure, even for a Temple, and all they've got in the backcountry is the odd healer and pilgrim shrine.

No offense, but your manners are a little... coarse. If you're ever in Ebonheart, take a lesson or two in etiquette from Lassinia Mussillius. She'll smooth off those rough edges, make you more presentable for high society. She lodges at the Six Fishes Tavern.

Your manners are pleasant enough - but there's always room to gilt a silver tongue like yours. If you're ever in Ebonheart, take a lesson or two in etiquette from Lassinia Mussillius. You'll be riding high in fine society in no time. She lodges at the Six Fishes Tavern.

I didn't get these catlike reflexes just by jumping across rooftops at night. Senyndie the Redguard taught me everything I know. If you're in Vivec, ask around for her down with the gladiators in the Arena quarter. She makes the dancing girls in Suran look like ogrims with two left feet.

I didn't get these catlike reflexes just by jumping across rooftops at night. Aerin the Bosmer taught me everything I know. If you're in Maar Gan, ask around for her at the Andus Tradehouse. She makes the dancing girls in Suran look like ogrims with two left feet.

Light Armor, more than any other style, requires skill and technique to get the most out of. Taking a direct blow wearing netch leather is a good way to die young. If you're ever in Maar Gan, ask around for Aerin at the Andus Tradehouse. Her dancing lessons aren't cheap, but they may just save your life.

Light Armor, more than any other style, requires skill and technique to get the most out of. Taking a direct blow wearing netch leather is a good way to die young. Ask around for Aerin at the Andus Tradehouse. Her dancing lessons aren't cheap, but they may just save your life.

There's not many who will teach you the secrets of brewing quality potions. You just end up training your own competition. But if you want to learn from a master, you can't do better than Abelle Chriditte. She's able to tease potent effects from the most ordinary of ingrediants. Last I heard, she had become something of a hermit, settling into one of those ruined Dunmer strongholds on the north of the Ashlands.

They say Gilyan Sedas can put a throwing knife through a cliff racer's eye at fifty paces. Most Morag Tong assassins only train their own, but I've heard Gilyan's happy to show anyone some moves if they've got the gold. He works out of the Balmora branch.

There's no one faster with a knife than Todwendy. A couple of Cammona Tong toughs were getting rough with her over by the bar. One moment, they're trying to grab her waist - the next, they're flopping around on the floor with slit throats like fish gasping for air. I didn't even *see* the knife in her hand.

I hear there's no one faster with a knife than Todwendy. Apparently, a couple of Cammona Tong toughs were getting rough with her over at the Lucky Lockup. One moment, they're trying to grab her waist - the next, they're flopping around on the floor with slit throats like fish gasping for air. Punters say they didn't even *see* the knife in her hand. She works freelance, but I know the Morag Tong would take her on if she showed any interest.

I hear there's no one faster with a knife than Todwendy. Apparently, a couple of Cammona Tong toughs were getting rough with her over at the Lucky Lockup in Balmora. One moment, they're trying to grab her waist - the next, they're flopping around on the floor with slit throats like fish gasping for air. Punters say they didn't even *see* the knife in her hand. She works freelance, but I know the Morag Tong would take her on if she showed any interest.

Eydis Fire-Eye, the Balmora Fighter's Guild steward, has a temper as red as her hair. And she's got the skill with an axe to back it up. You're with the Fighter's Guild, right? You might learn a thing or two from sparring with her.

Eydis Fire-Eye, the Balmora Fighter's Guild steward, has a temper as red as her hair. And she's got the skill with an axe to back it up. She only trains her own recruits though - so forget about sparring with her.

You might not think it to look at him, but no one slings a meaner hex than Erer Darothril. Some Telvanni tried to put him to the test when he first arrived in Sadrith Mora.The lucky ones came back with burns that took months to heal. They never found the bones of the others. He likes the fast company and strong drink at Muriel's Cornerclub.

When I was coming up as a crusader, no one cracked more daedra skulls than Ernse Llervu with her ebony staff. She's retired now, and prefers to pray and fast in seclusion at the Abbey of St. Delyn the Wise in Vivec. Approach her with politeness and humility, and perhaps she'll teach you what she knows.

There are those skilled in the art of restoration, and then there's Yakin Bael. Shattered limbs, deep infections, horrific blight diseases - there's doesn't seem to be anyone he can't help with those blessed hands of his. Yakin's not actually a member of the Temple, but he's so talented they let him lodge at the Chapel in Vos, free of charge.

The soldiers posted out in Fort Buckmoth are tough as old dreugh boots - they're the ones fighting the blighted monsters that escape the Ghostfence. And you can't get cut or wounded by those things - unless you want to get infected and go mad yourself. Shardie the Redguard teaches the new recruits how to block every blow, so they all come home alive.

Back in the day, there was no gladiator more graceful than Seanwen the Altmer. He wore a full suit of ebony platemail, but moved as though it were nothing but silk. He killed enough fighters to win his freedom - now he trains the new recruits down in the Arena Waistworks.

Seryne Relas has more power in her little finger than most Telvanni wizards accumulate in their lifetime. But she's smart enough to stay out of House politics, teaching quietly from her home in Tel Branora.

It can't be easy for Skink in Tree's Shade. The Telvanni have little respect for the Mages Guild at the best of times, and even less for Argonians like him. Yet Skink seems to have come to an understanding with their leaders - some, privately, even admit to respecting him. You ask me, you'll learn more about making friends and influencing people from Skink than any 'diplomat' posted in Ebonheart.

The Temple of Two-Moons Dance in Torval has, for many hundreds of years, been the finest training ground in all Tamriel for warriors of foot and fist. But Torval is far away, hidden deep in the jungle palaces and moon sugarcane gardens of Elsweyr. The best of the Dunmer students was a mer called Taren Omothan. But the Temple calls Taren a heretic, and he's gone into hiding. I don't know where to find him.

The Temple of Two-Moons Dance in Torval has, for many hundreds of years, been the finest training ground in all Tamriel for warriors of foot and fist. But Torval is far away, hidden deep in the jungle palaces and moon sugarcane gardens of Elsweyr. The best of the Dunmer students was a mer called Taren Omothan - he trains the priests here in the sacred art so we can better defend ourselves.

A smith is only as good as our tools allow us to be. Cheap repair hammers are fine for fixing iron in the field, but as soon as your weapons and armor get more sophisticated, you need better tools. And no one makes finer tools than Sirollus Saccus, down at the Hawkmoth Legion Garrison in Ebonheart.

Have you met a Buoyant Armiger yet? The bravest of their ranks is Mertis Falandas. He's stationed out with the Ghostgate garrison, so he's always fighting blighted monsters. One infected wound from those mad beasts, and days later you'll die feverish with corprus. That's why he fights with a spear - killing them safely at a distance.

Have you met a Buoyant Armiger yet? Those fetchers have wits as sharp as their blades - they love to recite riddles, songs and poetry. But don't mistake them for bards. When it comes to the art of war, they're deadly. I hear the best of their ranks is Ulms Drathen. No one crosses swords with him and lives. I believe he's stationed out with the Molag Mar garrison.

There's no lock devised by man or mer that is proof against Hecerinde's skills. The self-styled 'gentleman thief' is something of a legend in the criminal underworld - but he always manages to stay one step ahead of the law. He lives in the rougher part of Balmora, and only trains those who are already well-known in the Guild.

There's no lock devised by man or mer that is proof against Hecerinde's skills. The self-styled 'gentleman thief' is something of a legend in the criminal underworld - but he always manages to stay one step ahead of the law. He lives in the rougher part of Balmora, and only trains those with the right... connections, if you catch my drift.

Now old Tuls Valen, at the Ald-Ruhn Temple, likes to preach the sermons and instruct the new initiates in the mysteries of the Three. But Methal Seran, his chief exorcist, is the more powerful priest. He only trains senior members of the Temple in his sacred arts - but there's no ghost or demon that he couldn't banish back to Oblivion.

You're pretty light on your feet, %PCRace. But I'll wager you wouldn't be able to sneak up on old Wadarkhu over in Gnaar Mok. That rag-eared smuggler slips from shadow to shadow like he was born of smoke itself.

When it comes to drawing every last drop of power from a soul into an enchantment, I like to think I have some skill. But the artifacts crafted by the Altmer, Qorwynn? They're like nothing I've ever seen. Each one shows a brilliance bordering on madness. He went missing many years ago -  some say he was kidnapped by Daedra worshippers. Others say he *joined* them.

It's no secret the Telvanni have powerful wizards in their ranks. But often unaffiliated magic users will flock to Sadrith Mora, looking for an enchanted bargain, exotic ingrediants, or rare spells and scrolls. Ardarume the Altmer is currently lodging at the Gateway Inn doing just that. Her training isn't cheap, and she doesn't tolerate fools - but she's knows what she's talking about.

Outlanders like yourself have to get used to the ashstorms of our land. We mastered the sloped-roof hut a long time ago. And the craftsmen have perfected the resin mesh for windows and such. Got bull netch tarps for when they're expecting a real big fall - drape those on your dome for the night and just pull it all down in the morning or the next day.

Vivec cares for priest and pauper alike. Certainly the priests, Ordinators, and Buoyant Armigers meet with Vivec more often than others, but he is not aloof. Vivec cares deeply for all his people. Many outlanders who come here want to see Vivec, but he is not a circus or spectacle for your entertainment.

The Daedra are powerful ancestor spirits, similar to the blessed Tribunal, but weaker and more capricious. In the olden times, before the Advent of the Tribunal, the Daedra were worshipped as gods by the Chimer, but were undeserving of this veneration, as they harmed their followers as often as they helped them.

Khajiti men show their status in life with their names, unless they choose a nickname. "M" or "Ma" means "child" or "apprentice" or, in the vernacular, "virgin." As an apprentice can be of any age, this leads to misunderstandings and jokes %Name cannot translate. "J," Ji," or "Ja" means a bachelor or young adult. In the vernacular, it means one who is young and lacks experience. "Ra" and "Ri" show high status. "Ri" is the highest status among the Khajiit, used by leaders of cities or tribes.

Dunmer despise all other races. They seem to reserve a special passionate hatred of Altmer and Bosmer, but I've never seen slaves of either race - though I'm told they do exist. The Dunmer I know also avoid offending humans by keeping human slaves of any nation, although slaves with Nordic features are common enough in the north. The Dark Elves historically considered all beastpeoples and humans to be mere animals - it's only since Imperial times that they have grudgingly acknowledged humans as men.
I'm %Rank rank in the Guild, and I'd think twice about going down in a Daedric ruin without a crateful of potions and scrolls.

You want my advice, %PCRank? I've been around. I've risen to %Rank rank in the Guild by being smart and careful. And if I were you, I'd stay away from Daedric ruins until you have a little more experience, and a heftier kit bag.

Our plantations depend on slaves, mostly down south in Dres District, but here in the Ascadian Isles, too. It's our right to have slaves, by law and custom, and we'll fight for it on the Council till it makes good business sense to do otherwise.
Personally, I don't want slaves. No one I know has any. But it's our right to have slaves, by law and custom, and you outlanders must learn to respect the traditions of our people.

The Dark Elves say the Tribunal defeated Mehrunes Dagon himself in battle at the height of their powers. So, why didn't Vivec use his grand powers while fighting the Empire? If he can cause floods and hurl moons, as the stories say, why did he use just common troops and war strategies? Heh. Because they're just stories, that's why. Common sense, when you think about it - but the Dark Elves are a proud lot, you know how much their legends and superstitions mean to them.

If the Great Houses want a Dunmer noble dead badly enough, they'll get a contract through the Morag Tong. If the f'lah is smart, they flee the city; go underground and lay low for a spell. But some of the braver ones wait in ambush. They rarely survive.

What are the most dangerous places in Morrowind? Well, probably the ash vampire citadels inside the Ghostfence, on Red Mountain. But outside the Ghostfence? I guess the Daedric ruins would be the worst. They're all over the place, and full of bad Daedra, and the crazy folks who summon them. I hear vampires are pretty bad, too, but I've never seen any, personally.

Having served with the legions for many years, and having carried the Emperor's standard, I'd like to say he was universally loved and respected. But here in Vvardenfell, the Dunmer fight each other more than the Empire, and they all blame us when they do. That's what happens when you try to bring law and justice to Elves.

These Bosmer and Khajiit don't understand the nature or value of wealth. They certainly aren't loyal to the Emperor - but then no one is these days. It's not like it was when I first signed up for the Legions, let me tell you.

Every warrior worth his salt wants a suit of Ebony mail. We call it 'Godsblood' for good reason - you'll be defended as if the Three, bless their names, were watching over you. Of course, they say Daedric plate is even tougher - but evil spirits are trapped inside the metal during forging, and I want no part of that.

Every warrior worth his salt wants a suit of Ebony mail. The locals call it 'Godsblood' for good reason - you'll be defended as if the Divines themselves were watching over you. Of course, they say Daedric plate is even tougher - but evil spirits are trapped inside the metal during forging, and I want no part of that.

If you're sick, or drained, or diseased, then you can always find succor by praying at one of our shrines. You don't need to be one of our faith in order to receive the blessing of the Divines. Of course, such blessings are cheaper for the faithful - they do help to upkeep our shrines and spread the word of our faith through their actions and deeds, after all.

We welcome all races within the Imperial Cult. But most Dunmer natives cling to their worship of the Temple. I suppose they are more comfortable with Gods who can be seen, and speak to them in person. But Gods who take human form must also take on human imperfections. The Divines have no such flaws.

The Fighters Guild is a brotherhood of warriors. We provide a mercenary service to Morrowind, lending steel and shield to those who need our help. For the right price, of course. We're not a charity, and keeping our members trained and armed properly isn't cheap.

We are an Imperial Guild, serving the Emperor's law. Our members must have a clean criminal record. No contract will be accepted when it is offending the laws and customs of the realm. That means the contracts we can and can't take here can be very different than those we recieve in Cyrodiil.

Conjuration magic can be very useful for a warrior. No, I don't mean summoning beasts to fight your battles for you. But calling a Daedric weapon to your side gives you a powerful edge over your opponent. Few are lucky enough to own the genuine article - they're in the hands of wealthy collectors rather than adventurers these days.

You don't need to be as strong as an Orc to hit like one. There's a charm canny fighters use - amulets of 'mighty blows', we call them in the trade. Talk to Verick Gemain in Caldera - he's usually got something in stock, and his prices aren't extortionate either.

If you try and buy native armour here, they'll charge you outlander prices. It's a scribby trick, really - I know the watch are sitting on more suits of bonemold armour than they have guards to wear them. But will they loan it to us for sparring practice, or to protect new recruits out in the Ashlands? Vivec's charity, my backside - they'd rather it gathered dust in the storehouse than see foreigners like us wear it.

Lusting after a Daedric weapon? Forget about it, friend. Those things are in the hands of collectors, or under heavy lock and key. Tell you what, though. Ra'Virr, just down the street from here, sells the next best thing. Bound weapons still cost a shiny septim - but the old furball's got a 'sweet' tooth, if you know what I mean. Could be he'd give a discount if you slipped him a taste over the counter.
We turn to the ancestors for guidance. We honor them, and try to learn from the wisdom they impart to us.

The dead who guard our Ancestral Tombs are not the product of necromancy. They rise from love of kin or faith to duty, and so are not unholy. It is but the answering of the ancestors, the awakening of those who never sleep.

Here in Morrowind, we torch Conjurers and Necromancers right up on poles where they belong. Of course, now, the Telvanni wizards, they're different - like the Altmeri sorcerers, private in their towers and private in their affairs. Don't know much about them, and frankly, I don't want to.
There is no surer sign of decay in a land than to see the rites of religion held in contempt.

Everybody can learn a few spells. You don't need to be a wizard to cast spells. It makes life easier. A little light when you run out of candles, or a charm cantrip when the shopkeeper starts to raise his prices. And when you learn a spell, practice. It's the only way to learn, and it helps to pass the time.

There have been only a few rare incidents of the Mages Guild actually becoming involved in local political struggles. On these occasions, the Guild's participation has been the ultimate decider in the conflict.

If you want to trap a soul, summon the beast yourself, or purchase a scroll from someone who can. That way you make sure you are properly prepared and can defeat the creature on your own terms. Soultrapping down in Daedric Ruins is brave, but reckless, and likely to get you killed.

Before the Guild came here, magic was the preserve of the few. All the Houses had their mages, of course, and villages might have had a hedgewizard or two. But nothing respectable. Conjurers and warlocks were branded necromancers - hunted down and burnt at the stake by the Temple.
Necromancy is inherently dangerous. A mage cannot 'dabble' in it. The simplest spell requires the spilling of blood, and immediately begins to corrupt the caster's soul.

Ranis Athrys had something against wizards who aren't in the guild. It's not a surprise really - her parents were murdered by the old Telvanni Archmagister, the one before Gothren. I guess one of them caught up with her in the end.
Ranis Athrys has something against wizards who aren't in the guild. It's not a surprise really - her parents were murdered by the old Telvanni Archmagister, the one before Gothren.
Death smiles at us all. All a man can do is smile back.
Death smiles at us all. All a mer can do is smile back.
Friends and wealth do not hold much joy for me. Yet the thrill of the chase, the grace of the kill; these are things that can still move me to laughter or tears.

Usually, I like to paralyse my target before striking the killing blow. Safer, and my victim feels no pain. Which means no sound, no alarm, no guards. With one exception. Never, ever, try such a technique on a vampire. Something about their dark pact makes the nightwalkers immune to that magic. They'll tear your throat out in a heartbeat, given that opening.
The Great Houses are in a state of silent, shadowed war, of secret poisons, artful daggers and sleeping men strangled in their beds.

I shouldn't be saying this too loud, so listen close. No one LIKES Archmagister Gothren. But no one gets to vote for the Telvanni archmagister, either. The archmagister only changes when someone kills the old archmagister. There's no one in a position to challenge him now. And Gothren has spies in every city that make sure no one starts to plot against him.

Argonians generally make for better slaves than the Khajiit. They have natural resistances to disease and poison, meaning you can work them harder, longer and in more dangerous conditions without losing your property.

Always pull a catman's lips back and check the teeth before you make a purchase. If they're black, that usually means the beast is addicted to moonsugar. Don't let the slavemasters flog you an addict slave - not at full price, anyway.

House Telvanni used to rely on Redoran mercenaries for protection and security. Now the Vvardenfell Mage-Lords are expanding their territory, we've been forced to turn to Western mercenaries for guards and agents. That's the reason you see so many outlanders swelling our ranks for the moment.

House Telvanni used to rely on Redoran mercenaries for protection and security. Now the Vvardenfell Mage-Lords are expanding their territory, they're turning to Western mercenaries for guards and agents. Lucky for us, eh %PCName?

Archmagister Gothren doesn't live in Sadrith Mora. That might seem unusual for the head of the House, but when you think of all the scheming wizards and assassins for hire in the city, you see it's a precaution. A more isolated tower is a more secure tower, and far easier to defend.

It is safer to be feared than loved, if you cannot be both. Where charm or bribery fails, you can always intimidate your target into submission. They'll remember the slight should you ever need to call upon them again, however.
A wealthy mer can afford anything except a conscience.

In the conservative south, the Indoril parties and the Temple still have a lot of influence in the Councils, but up north, Imperial influence is strong, and Hlaalu family and retainers control most of the wealth and political power. Of course, within their own territories, each of the five Great Houses rule their local councils - but the power of Hlaalu and Imperial coin is very influential.
Every mer has his price, %PCName. Even friendship is for sale.
The earth of Vvardenfell is rich with veins of ebony and diamond. Fame and fortune would be piled upon the lucky f'lah who discovered fresh deposits for their House.

The nobles of House Hlaalu are great merchant princes. A wealthy individual has already proven their worth by turning fortune into profit. But they are also mer of means - able to invest in and expand the clan, with great resources at their disposal.

We've cast our lot with the Empire. Our fortunes will wax and wane with theirs. The Telvanni, on the other hand, have simply ignored Imperial law to secure their position. I'm talking about these rogue settlements, where mages disguised as pilgrims are dropped off by caravans all over the ashlands.

The glory of the Indoril is long in the past. They once used their control of the Tribunal priesthood to dominate the other Houses, but their hegemony was overthrown during the Armistice, never to recover.
I have never seen Vivec myself, but I have felt his presence. I know that he loves his people and protects us. He is no far-away idea like these uncaring Imperial gods, but flesh and blood.
Death comes for us all, in the end. Sadly, we cannot choose how, but we can decide how we meet that end; and so the manner in which we are remembered.

Do not laugh at serious matters, for it shows disrespect. Do not spread rumors, for they fester and will in turn be spread about you. Reputation among our people is hard-earned, over time. But once gained, you have it for life.

Did you hear Bolvyn Venim killed another outlander in a duel? The man was an officer in the House Guard, but Bolvyn Venim insulted his ancestors at a meal, so of course the officer had to demand satisfaction. And of course he had no chance against Venim. He may be lacking in honour - but certainly not courage.

Khajiit are all loyal citizens and we all love the Emperor very, very much. The Mane seems powerful in Elsweyr, yes, but you forget the city governments, the chiefs of the tribes, the Clan Mothers. It is all very complicated at home, and %Name does not want to bore the %PCRace.

We take our holy days very seriously. Triune - what you folk celebrate as New Life - we sit all day at Temple listening to the lay fellows reading lessons from the lives of the saints. Holidays are more a duty than a frolic. Ancestor's Day is a pleasant reunion around the clan hearth - comfortable with friends and family, quiet, and respectful of the hearth spirits -- good foods and small gifts. That's Tales and Tallows for you outlanders, and all your superstitious nonsense about evil spirits and ghosts.
It's bad enough with the blight storms this year, but the Ashlanders are also going crazy, jumping caravans and pilgrims, raiding villages. They ought to send the Legions out and teach them a lesson.
Now that Dagoth Ur has fallen, perhaps the Temple will dismantle the Ghostfence, and let our ancestors who fuel it finally rest in peace.
The last Buoyant Armiger assault against Red Mountain ended in defeat. They retreated and most survived, but since then we've relied on the Ghostfence to keep Dagoth Ur and his hordes at bay.

Outlanders like yourself are always wondering how long we Dunmer live to. It's no great secret, really. I'm fifty, done over thirty years in the fields, and I'm in the prime of life. I expect another fifty good years, and then I'll be old, and slow, chatting with gaffers around the hearth for another twenty, thirty years. I've known mer still mind-sharp in their late hundreds, and even heard of folk two hundred and older.

The Great Houses tend to favour certain races as mercenaries. House Hlaalu employs the brute muscle of Nords and Orcs. The Redoran admire the skill and discipline of the Redguard. Even the reclusive Telvanni have many Altmer and Bosmer in their pay.

Be careful before you get into bed with a particular faction. There is usually a competitor or ideological opposite to any one House or Guild - so find out who your new enemies will be before you pledge your allegiance.

The Temple of Two-Moons Dance in Torval has for many hundreds of years been the finest training ground in all Tamriel for warriors of foot and fist. But Torval is far away, hidden deep in the jungle palaces and symmetrical moon sugarcane gardens of Elsweyr. The best of the Dunmer students was Taren Omothan. But the Temple calls Taren a heretic, and so he is in hiding. I do not know where to find him.

Have you met a Buoyant Armiger yet? They keep their wits as sharp as their blades - they love riddles, song and poetry. But don't mistake them for bards. When it comes to the art of war, they're deadly. And none more so than the crusader Ulms Drathen. I've never seen a man more skilled with a sword. He's stationed out with the Molag Mar garrison, I believe.

Now, old Tuls Valen at the Ald-Ruhn Temple likes to preach the sermons and instruct the new initiates in the mysteries of the Three. But Methal Seran, his chief exorcist, is probably the more powerful priest. He only trusts senior members of the Temple to teach his sacred arts to - but there's no ghost or demon that won't bend the knee when Methan Seran issues the command.
You're pretty light on your feet, %PCRace. But you wouldn't be able to surprise old Wadarkhu over in Gnaar Mok. That smuggler slips from shadow to shadow like he was born of smoke itself.

Red Mountain dominates the minds and spirits of we Dunmer, looming high above the horizon in all northern settlements. It is sacred, and a site of pilgrimages - that is, folk travel to shrines on its remote flanks, but the Ghostfence prevents any travel to the peak and crater themselves.
Khajiit respect men and mer, but we do not wish to be compared to them. These Dunmer do no not know that calling %Name 'bald' or 'unclawed,' is a deadly insult!
Khajiit respect men and mer, but we do not wish to be compared to you. Calling a Khajiit, even an Ohmes-Khajiit, 'bald' or 'unclawed,' is a deadly insult.

It is good to see another marshsister out here in Morrowind. Too many of us sleep, work and eat in chains under the hateful eye of the slavers. I want to see them free. And I want to see the Dunmer freed of their bone-headed dogma that says we are little better than beasts.

It is good to see another marshbrother out here in Morrowind. Too many of us sleep, work and eat in chains under the hateful eye of the slavers. I want to see them free. And I want to see the Dunmer freed of their bone-headed dogma that says we are little better than beasts.

Always good to meet another Breton out here. I do so miss the music of our native High Rock! The nyckelharpa with its solemn strings - brings me to tears every time. Can't say I miss the politics, though. Our backstabbling noble families make the Dunmer look positively civilised by comparison.

I can't tell you how refreshing it is to see a fellow Altmer. Finally, some sophisticated discourse! Please, don't be a stranger - I find the scope of my mind and manners dried out - nay, malnourished! - to that of a bejar-nut out here.

You're out on the frontier now, my friend. You won't find any of the finer things you may have been used to back in Cyrodiil. The wine made from comberry - 'shein', they call it - is bitter, nasty stuff. If you're expecting a bottle of Tamika wine with your tavern meal - even the cheaper vintages - forget it. Imperial brandy is the only taste of home that seems to have been imported since the Armistice.

A couple of hardy Nords like us could take on near any challenge this land might throw at us. The Redoran are fine enough warriors - but they're more used to ritual duels than the bloody crash and thunder of war. Only the Buoyant Armigers, out on the frontier at Ghostgate, really live by the sword-edge of life and death - fighting those deformed monsters of Dagoth Ur.

These Dunmer can't craft metal worth a damn. Sure, the shellsmiths do clever, intricate work with bone and resin - but if you want a blade worthy of a true Orc, you'll need to shop around. Go see Garothmuk gro-Muzgub, the smith in Suran - he'll get you sorted out. I hear the Legion smith in Ebonheart is pretty good, too - but I haven't been there myself.

Remember that old Hammerfell saying; 'A man is only a great as the beard that wears him?' Well, you won't see much of that round here. A big beard is seen as unfashionable at best, and dirty or beggarish at worst. So most Redguards in Morrowind I know go around clean-shaven, just to rub along. I wonder if it goes back to the ancient Dunmer rivalry with the Dwemer? They had magnificent beards, if the statues are anything to go by.

If you're expecting some sort of warm welcome from our gloomy, taller kin, forget about it. They care as little for us as they do their Imperial overlords or the so called 'beast' races. Don't be surprised to hear 'thief' or 'cannibal' muttered when you walk into a tavern. The land itself is just as unforgiving - as soon as you set foot beyond the Ascadian Isles or the swamps on the coast, don't expect to see a single tree that hasn't been ravaged by the ashstorms down to a stump.
If you want to make a friend, keep your weapon sheathed. Moving your hand to the hilt of your weapon - even resting your palm on the pommel - can be seen as a formal challenge in some situations.

Veneration of the Eight Divines and Tiberius Imperator has gained some local acceptance, particularly among House Hlaalu, but the Tribunal Temple is and always has been the one and only state religion of Morrowind.

We don't much love foreigners here in Vvardenfell, and we don't thank you for interfering. A people should keep to their own, if you take my meaning. And that's not the Empire's way. I look around, I don't see much benefit from uniting the provinces, unless you're a fatcat merchant, or maybe a soldier.
Do you remember that old saying from Black Marsh, %PCName? That the best soil for a seed is found in your heart.
There is an old saying from Black Marsh, outlander. That the best soil for a seed is found in your heart.

Some Daedra, like Gods to the other cultures, are sacred to the Dunmer. They even consider Boethiah as the first of their kind. I'll grant that, to strangers, it may seem odd that the Dunmer hold the darker powers in esteem. Rest assured though; there is more to Morrowind than just a heathen den of demon-worshippers.

The Houses play out what we Dunmer call the 'Great Game'. The Morag Tong is a tool in the hands of the Great Houses, in the unending competition for honor, glory and power. According to the Mephala Entente, anyone may be marked, from the High Hlaalu himself to the lowliest Telvanni serf. Non-Dunmer are forbidden to hire or to be marked; some say that Tiber Septim himself negotiated this arrangement with the Morag Tong at the time of the Armistice.

The Empire has conquered through power, armies and strength. Yet what they build in peace, they draw from Altmer ideas, civilisation and intellect. Even the common tongue of the Empire, Tamrielic, is based on our speech and writing. And it is a poor imitation, if I may say so.

Some Redorans think they know better than the Emperor what's right and wrong, if you take my meaning. And I've heard it said that the Hlaalu adopted Imperial culture, but I've never seen such a lazy, selfish, backstabbing lot in my life. As for the Telvanni, well, they're wizards - and I don't like wizards.

'Dar' in a Khajiiti name means 'thief,' but this should not alarm you. 'Dar' is like the Nordic 'Clever Hudvar' or the Breton 'Arnand the Fox.' A Khajiit with 'Dar' in his name is clever, and maybe clever with his hands, but not always a thief by odd Imperial property customs.
In Skyrim, it is an old tradition to rub canis root on the trees surrounding your house as a ward against werebears.

Iron and steel are easy to repair. Just heat them up and pound them back into shape. You can even use a camp fire in a pinch. Ebony can only be hammered when heated. It develops small cracks that eventually shatter the material if hammered cold. Now I hear Daedric should always be worked on at night... ideally under a new or full moon, and never during an eclipse. A red harvest moon is supposed to be best.

Many Redguards serve as mercenaries in House Redoran. It's not just that we make talented swordsmen, but we share a similar outlook on life. The rocky deserts of Hammerfell are tough and unforgiving, much like the Ashlands where the Redoran make their home. So we understand that life is hard-fought, and hard-earned.
In Valenwood, we have a penalty for trespassing - one bone broken for every twig snapped underfoot.

We Bosmer have long been misunderstood as outcasts. It stems from the 'Green Pact' we make with our God - in part of which we promise to eat the meat of our fallen foes. This disgusts other races, and so they call us cannibals and savages. They do not understand that this is how we show respect for nature, and the body of the enemy - wasting neither meat, nor bone, nor fur.

Not only can a nimble acrobat leap to places others cannot, they also have a better sense of balance and control. When you can climb the steep slopes, you'll uncover the secrets hidden across the mountains in Vvardenfell.
Take care when using Telvanni bugmusk, or any other magic that makes you more charming. No one likes being used, and your new friend will realise they've been tricked after that sweet haze wears off.

Casting a fireball might look flashy, but it's a foolish Mage who relies upon it here. Use your head, outlander. You're in Morrowind. Our homeland. We shrug off the heat. Folks say it comes from years of living under the sweltering shadow of Red Mountain.

Casting a fireball might look flashy, but it's a foolish Mage who relies upon it here. Use your head, %PCRace. You're in Morrowind. Land of the Dunmer. And Dunmer are naturally resistant to heat. Catch my drift?
Any hedge wizard can burn up his enemies with fire. Yet destroying your enemy so directly should be the last resort of a skilled battlemage.

There's no harm in sleeping rough, and eating what you can find. Living off the land. Anywhere outside of town you can just lay down under the stars and take your rest -- provided there aren't any thieves or kagouti around.

Wielding a mace is all about timing and momentum. Once the swing of the mace has begun, stopping it or slowing it down is difficult. The fighter commits not just to the blow, but also the recoil. Begin your strike when the opponent is leaning forward, hopefully off balance. It is completely predictable that he will lean backward, so aim for a point behind his head. By the time the mace gets there, his head will be in its path.

Every creature, living or dead, is powered by a soul. Without it, they are just lumps of flesh or piles of bones. This animating force can be contained within a soul gem, if the soul gem has the capacity. From the gem, the power can be used to power magical items.

The key to unarmed combat is concentration. All of the blow is concentrated into a small point. Therefore it is more potent. To strike with just the thumb can be more deadly than to strike with the whole fist. However, only the highly trained fighter can do this.
Even if you were born common, you can attempt to conduct yourself like gentry. Learn the law and local customs. If you don't mind your manners, you'll get called out to a duel.

You'll need plenty of levitation potions if you want to do business with House Telvanni. You can brew your own from the trama root, racer plumes, or coda flowers. A thick, bitter-tasting root of the trama shrub grows in the Ashlands, Molag Amur, and Red Mountain regions. Racer plumes are plucked from dead cliff racers. Coda flowers are collected from the draggle-tail plant which blooms in swampland.

Levitation potions can be produced from the trama root, racer plumes, and coda flowers. A thick, bitter-tasting root of the trama shrub grows in the Ashlands, Molag Amur, and Red Mountain regions. Racer plumes are plucked from dead cliff racers. Coda flowers are collected from the draggle-tail plant which blooms in swampland.

To cure common diseases, combine gravedust and green lichen. Gravedust is spirit-affinitive dust taken from remains buried in consecrated ground. Green lichen is a hardy primitive plant that grows on the rocks around the West Gash.
Stay away from the mudcrabs. Swamp Fever starts with a slight temperature, but you'll be raving and delirious by the end. Go join the Tribunal Temple. Initiates get free Cure Disease at the shrines.

Take care around sickened creatures. The bite of a diseased Alit or Kagouti is unusually vicious, and their frenzied brains cannot feel pain. Even if the beast is dead, the disease lingers upon the carcass. Many hunters come to me for healing after they strip meat and hides from sick beasts.

Invisibility is one of the most prized of all potions. They can be made only from crushed diamonds and bittergreen petals. Diamonds are expensive, and Bittergreen only flowers around Red Mountain, where few dare to travel.

Wortcraft is what we call eating raw magical ingredients. When you grind herbs and roots against the teeth, it occasionally releases its simplest essence and results in a fleeting effect on the eater.

Common thieves will stick a dagger in an opponent's back. This may slay the target, but more often gives him time to scream and drenches the attacker with blood. Not good. A throat-slash, properly executed, can both slay and silence a guard, while leaving your clothes unstained.
There is a profit to be made from death. Not only can you rob the deceased, but, if your victim has enemies, which rich people often do, you can be paid even more for it.

The blight storms have been so bad around Red Mountain this year that my crops and herds are really suffering. I'm going to have to put my prices up, and the product I'll be selling will taste more like ash than last season.

You did not just defeat Dagoth Ur, my friend. You healed the very land we depend on. Since the ash has stopped raining from Red Mountain, our fields have been blooming like never before. The harvest will be plentiful this year, and my crops will taste cleaner and sweeter than I or my ancestors can ever remember.
While silver weapons are slightly less durable than steel, they have the unique ability to wound ghosts and Daedric monsters.
The primitive burial customs of the Dunmer are nothing but foolish superstitions. Only we hold sway over life and death.

Casting Alteration spells is convincing a greater power that it will be easier to change reality than to resist the push of your command. Reality is like wind and water. It cannot be removed. But it can be bent, channeled, or redirected.

Most Dunmer fear and despise vampires in equal measure. The Temple preaches that they are the unholy spawn of the Daedric prince Molag Bal. Personally, I don't believe vampires are anything to be feared with the right magic at my disposal.

Most Dunmer fear and despise vampires in equal measure. The Temple preaches that they are the unholy spawn of the Daedric prince Molag Bal. However, from an arcane standpoint, their powers do make for a fascinating study.

You'd be surprised at how many 'honest' shipmasters make deals on the side with entrepreneurs like myself. The average passenger has no idea that the ships they sail aboard have cargo holds stuffed full of moon sugar, skooma and Dwemer artifacts.
Sure, I get some hard-cases and dark-eyed mages on my ship from time to time. But I'll take smugglers and those rogue Telvanni anywhere they want to go, as long as their gold is good.
Get some rest before selling your treasures or looking for a bargain at the market. If a Merchant senses the customer is tired and looking for a quick deal, they will take advantage of you.

The trickiest of all armours to repair is Glass. Hammer blows struck across the grain run the risk of shattering the armor. Same goes with weapon blows. So make sure you always carry your own hammers if you protect yourself with Glass.

Warhammers and Battle Axes may feel slow to swing, but they're deadly in the hands of a trained fighter. The heavier your weapon, the more it will literally club down your opponent, causing them to stagger, and interrupting their own attacks.

We don't tolerate necromancers here, outlander. They steal the bones of our fathers and treasure from our tombs. The wise spirits of our ancestors are forced into their service like slaves and beasts. That's why the Temple hunts them down and burns them at the stake.

Some rough customers come into town now and then for supplies. I reckon they're smugglers and bandits holed up in the caves and mines hereabouts. Me, I'm no fighter, I just keep my head down. But an adventurer like yourself could go and clean them out. Might make yourself some gold while you're at it.
Find out where the Camonna Tong drink around town. Then stay away from those places. They don't like outlanders, except under building foundations.

The Thieves Guild and the Camonna Tong are in a Guild War for control of Vvardenfell. The Camonna Tong are the ancient Dunmer syndicate. They hate foreigners, and always will. If they win, there'll be no place for you here, outlander.
Stay clear of the Camonna Tong. They don't like outlanders, and what they don't like, they kill.

Folks say poison is a woman's weapon - but then again, most folk are fools. If you can't cast the spell yourself, find a smith who sells weapons imbued with the stuff. Most bandits and highwaymen are too hard up or plain foolhardy to carry a cure around with them.

Keep a scroll or two of Turn Undead to hand when raiding tombs. Anything dead and dangerous will flee from the magic, leaving you free to loot Dunmer heirlooms at your own pace. Don't boast to the natives afterwards though - it could be their great-great grandfather's possessions you've got in your sack.
Big cities like Ald Ruhn, they have the Sweeps, a guild of broom-handlers who make good money cleaning up after the ashstorms. Round here it's harder to make a drake for a day's hard graft.
Darts and throwing knives don't pack much of a punch, but they're lightweight, easily concealed and leave you with a free hand for a shield or torch.

People say we Dunmer are too 'serious'. Well, it's true you won't see us carrying on like you outlanders. Not in public, and not much in private either. Cutting up the fool, drinking and the like... well, it just doesn't seem proper to me.
%Name hides no secrets from the %PCRace.
You pry too much, outlander. Where are your manners?
Why would I share my secrets with you?
If you see a Nord with a nasty scar running down his face on the road, steer clear. He's a killer with a heart of stone.
Okur says she's being haunted by some spirit or ghost by night. It's hogwash, of course - she's probably been at the mazte, and the swamp heat is playing tricks on her.

Nine-holes may seem like a fun way to cut loose - but take care. Plenty of those games are rigged by the Hlaalu - and even if you *think* you've got the table licked, the house always wins in the end. Just ask Murudius.

The Imperial Cult sent their crusaders to Ashalmawia, said they burnt out those witches root and branch. But the fisherfolk say there are still strange lights flickering down there on a clear night. I'd steer clear, if I was you.
Endris has been off the boil lately. Shouts in his shack, sometimes all through the night. If he wants to hit the mazte, that's his business - but he needs to know his limits.
Morvayn Manor was overrun by corprus monsters. I thought they couldn't get out of the Ghostfence?

Out there, beyond the Ghostfence, stumble beasts mad with corprus. They inhabit the old Dwemer ruins and dwell in the dark of our burned-out fortresses. They kidnap the lone wanderer, harry our caravans, and when they are bold, they attack our towns. I've heard its only been getting worse of late.

Same, old, same old. Summers are short, the ash storms are long. The towns are overcrowded. Food is expensive, because little grows from the volcanic soil. Guilds control trade; nobles control the taxes. Life goes on.

Typical outlander. Sniffing around for opportunity and treasure, no doubt. %PCClass, you call yourself? I'd call you a scoundrel, a sword-for-hire, a cutthroat. No need for your sort around here, that's the truth of it.
Khajiit has no time for this. Why won't the %PCRace leave us alone?
This idle prattle bores me, s'wit.
I don't gossip with the likes of you.
A terrible thing.

It's no secret we find you greedy and opportunistic - that any morals or traditions you might have had come second to business. Your retainers are masters of blackmailing and backstabbing, both literal and metaphorical. While a few of your councilors may be honest and fair, most are under-handed and corrupt. I'm sure you don't enjoy hearing this - but it is the truth, all the same.

House Hlaalu are greedy and opportunistic, and any morals or traditions they might have had come second to business. Hlaalu retainers are masters of blackmailing and backstabbing, both literal and metaphorical. While a few councilors may be honest and fair, most are under-handed and corrupt. Take care when dealing with them.

You Hlaalu serve profit blindly. Yes, your masters are fast talkers and intelligent traders - but this is their greatest liability. Most of you are bribable, either with gold or with other favors. Your leaders are no exception.

House Hlaalu serve profit blindly. This is their great strength - they are fast talkers and intelligent traders - and their greatest liability. Most Hlaalu are bribable, either with gold or with other favors. Their leaders are no exception.
How tactless, %PCRace. You backward Redorans couldn't barter the muck off a mudcrab.
No, Q-u-a-t-e-rnary variations. Geological energies. How can I put this in a manner you Guild simpletons can understand? Magic-in-the-rocks. Now take your scuttlebrain flattery elsewhere.
My magics are far beyond the understanding of your narrow-minded Guild.
A girl like me deserves to work with better hides? Puurlease, outlander.

Personally, %PCName, I know you to be a %PCRace of honor. I'm sure you must have had your reasons to do what you've done. But you are a notorious outlaw, and until you have cleared your name, or paid your debt to society, it stains my reputation to be seen with you.
Personally, %PCName, I know you to be a good soul. But you are a notorious outlaw, and until you have cleared your name, or paid your debt to society, I cannot be seen to be your friend.

Personally, %PCName, I really respect you. But you are a notorious outlaw, and I serve the Emperor and his laws. I could be discharged from the army for not taking you in. So, I'm going to pretend I didn't see you...

It's hard to believe someone of your stature in the Guild could be in so much trouble with the law, %PCRank. Please, turn yourself in or clear your name before you bring us into further disrepute. Respectable patrons won't fund my studies if they know I associate with you.

Look, %PCRank. With such a high price on your head, everyone assumes you are a murderer. I don't know the details, and don't want to know. But we're an Imperial Guild, and we won't be getting paid contracts if our ranking members can't follow the law.

Vehk's teeth, I love a proper storm like this! I'm happy as any Nord to sail under mighty winds, outlander. Just tell me your destination, and we'll cast off for open waters.
Nothing like a good lashing of rain to make you feel alive, I say. Where are you headed, friend? Looking for a ship to take you there?
I'm Ebonheart's shipmaster. Looking for a short sail to Vivec? Shores more distant, perhaps? It's a clear enough night, so we'll steer by the stars.
A pleasant morning to you, friend. I'm Ebonheart's shipmaster. Looking for a short sail to Vivec? Shores more distant, perhaps?
Hai, outlander! What's your destination? Foul weather, I know - but the strider doesn't get spooked by a little thunder and lightning. She's a tough old thing.
Hail, outlander. Let's not get soaked to the britches, eh? Tell me your destination quick, and we can get you under the blankets at the back.
Ride and slumber? Or gaze up at the heavens on our journey? The choice is yours - just tell me your destination.
Good morning, outlander. I'm Balmora's caravaner. Tell me your destination, and I'll tell you if I can help you.
You lost in the mist, traveller? Or looking for a silt strider? Tell me your destination.
Ho there, outlander! Almost missed you in all this scribby-scree. What's your destination? Don't worry, there's shelter under the shell to keep you from the worst of this.
Nothing quite like a stroll after dark, is there? Planning a journey by starlight? What's your destination?
A fine evening to you, outlander. I'm the caravaner for Ald'ruhn. Planning a journey? What's your destination?
Good morning, outlander. I'm the caravaner for Ald'ruhn. Planning a journey? What's your destination?
You're a sweet thing, eh %PCRace? Looking for a sharp f'lah to show you a good time, I'll bet. Come closer - I don't bite.
You're a sharp one, eh %PCName? Looking to let off some steam I'll wager. I know a lot of nice ladies round town. Happy to introduce a smart gent like yourself, for the right price.
I'm easy to miss sera. That slip of a girl with a voice like a wisp of silk. Then you miss your purse of septims; but when you look for me, I'm no longer there.
Me? Well, I'm a poor lover, a worse gambler, and a fantastic drinker. Pleased to meet you, %PCRace.
I was born on the deck of a ship and raised with the salt breeze in my face. I've been toughened since with the experience of a hundred ports and desert islands.
You're a curious sort of f'lah, eh? Lets just say when you sink a lot of ships, it's easy to find sunken treasure.
I'm %Name. I've got my fingers in a few pies at the moment. You need something others can't get - you come see me.
I'm just a sharp f'lah who likes a game of nine holes or two. You play yourself %PCRace?
I'm a professional locksmith, me. You want a spare pair of keys fixed up, just in case like, might be I could help you.
You'll find me in the slums and the cornerclubs. What others see as squalor and menace in narrow cobbled alleys is home to me.
I'm a secretive and restless sort - always one step ahead of the hangman's noose.
%Name, pleased t'meetcha. I'm a jeweller. A diamond girl, right? So you got any gems you need looked at, or after, you come see me.
I am %name, %class of the %faction.
I am %name, a noble of %faction.
My past is not for the telling, sera. It is in deeds, not words. A life is only measured by the lives it saves.
The power of my faith is quiet, sera. It is the leaf unmoved by the hurricane.

I am a crusader, a warrior with a cause. So heed my words, traveler. Plagues, war, desolation . . . all these are mere glimpses of what is yet to come from Red Mountain's vault of horrors. It will take more than steel alone to purge this world of Dagoth-Ur and his devilkin.
Some warriors protect the meek and innocent. I, %Name, seek out and smite evil wherever it lurks.
I'm a crusader of House Redoran. My mighty sword-hand is anchored by holy purpose.

I am a %rank of House Redoran. I fight the warped beasts that stumble out of the blight storm. I know the day will come when I face a battle I cannot win. But I will greet that day as I have any other.

I am %name, a warrior of House Redoran. Sometimes a warrior dies a glorious death with his sword held high. But I've seen enough combat to know that sometimes, you're just target practice. Life can be cruel, and death won't change that.
Best leave your tongue in its yap-hole, Hlaalu scum. Your silvered words and golden bribes do not sparkle so brightly outside Balmora.
I am %name, a warrior of the Redoran. A fool knows no fear - but a warrior merely shows no fear. Which are you, I wonder?
I am a soldier of House Redoran, a sword of Vivec. I strike without fear, for his mind has divined how my foes will be slain.
Ser %name, at your service. From the moment I swore the oath to House Redoran, I belonged to my lord, sword and soul. That is all you need to know.
Battle tempers soldiers as fire tempers steel. I am ser %name, and I crave neither scars nor glory - simply humble service to my clan and the Three, blessed be thy names.

I am %rank %name. An outlander like yourself cannot possibly comprehend the arcane powers I do. I will merely say this. True strength is in the mind, for the body is too fragile a form. A word here, a gesture there, and it crumbles to dust.

I know many spells, outlander. The commands that bend beasts and Daedra to my will. The words that freeze the blood mid-flow and the heart mid-beat. Spells to make you remember. Spells to help you forget.

The common mer fears sorcerers like myself, for people always fear what they do not understand. Morrowind is a haunted place - plagued by rogue spirits and cunning demons alike. To walk this shadowy world without knowledge of the arcane is to walk unarmed into the lair of the enemy.
I am a sorcerer, a seeker of arcane knowledge. I have held ancient books as they slowly crumbled, secrets turning to dust. But their every word still sings in my head.
Two kinds of mer survive in this world - the powerful, and those who stay close to them. Stay close to House Telvanni, and perhaps even you can make something of yourself.

My minions rise from their graves to bend the knee. Dunmer superstition calls this 'necromancy'. I have no love for the Imperial yoke - but did you know in their homeland, you may legally purchase bodies and souls for private experimentation? It is most intriguing.

I study the arcane arts, of course. For what? For power. What else is there? Not just the power of the Emperor or his legions but the power to boil a man’s blood in his veins. To call on the thunder of the sky and the churn of the roiling earth! To shrug off the rules the world holds so dear.

Morrowind may appear on the surface to be a chaotic array of warring factions and clans to an outlander like yourself. Yet it has a beautiful order to those who are able to see it - glistening like a spider's web of connections, favours, vendettas and secrets that bind us all together. I am one of those that sit in the centre of the web, plucking its strands for the wizards-lords of House Telvanni.

It's said that the prime substance of the world is not matter or mana, but lies. Everything we do, everything we value - lies we tell each other, lies we tell ourselves. The world is fabrication, %PCRace - a convenient story to help us sleep at night. I'm just a particularly skilled storyteller, working for my House.

I am a %rank of House Hlaalu. But please, don't treat me like royalty. The easy prey is the powerful noble grown lazy, thinking themselves beyond the reach of danger. A good nightblade like myself know that anyone - from the slave in her cell to the lord in his castle - can be killed.
I am %name. Please excuse my bold stare. All mer look like prey to the eyes of an old nightblade.
I am %name. Please excuse my bold stare. All people look like prey to the eyes of an old nightblade.
I am %name. Silent as a shadow, and just as hard to flee. Don't let that put the frighters on you, %PCName. Stick around, I'll show you some of what I know.
I am %name. Silent as a shadow, and just as hard to flee.
I'm what they call a nightblade. That means I can put a dagger in your neck in the blink of an eye. Best not blink, eh?
I'm %name, a Hlaalu agent. What makes me so good at my job? Well, the trick isn't setting up the trade. It's making each side think it got the better deal.
I'm %name. I make a living selling rumors, lies, forgeries, or - if you can pay highly enough - the truth.
All conflict is best settled by compromise my friend. I am %name, a Hlaalu lawyer and a scholar.
I'm a soldier for House Hlaalu, and my master pays handsomely. Loyalty to coin is loyalty nonetheless.
I'm a Hlaalu sellsword. Follow your passion, I always say. Might as well get paid to do what you love.
Our agents calculate the amount of tribute we are due. I measure out the punishment for delinquency.
I am %name the %class. I've cast my lot with the reds.

%name is a good servant, and loyal to her master.
%name is a good servant, and loyal to his master.

%name is strong of arm and sharp of claw. Sometimes the ashskins think %name is their slave, to fetch this food or pour that drink. %name leaves these fools with a cut here, or bone broken there. A friendly warning, yes?
%name lives here as free Khajiit. No chains or beatings for %name, no sera.
%name lives here as free Khajiit. Own home, own hearth.
%name, at your service sera. I own this place.
%name, at your service my friend. I own this place.
